rho_reference_assessment.protocol: note section 9.5 item 6 (E19) and section 9.13 (E24): the whole run priced in F_p multiplications against the matched negation walk on the same curve, 16 negation and 16 unfolded walks per curve; ratio = total_muls / mean fp_muls of the 16 negation walks (set-up included).
rho_reference_assessment.matches_protocol: every record carries 16 negation and 16 unfolded walks, all correct; rho_matched_muls equals the mean of the negation walks' fp_muls and ratio = total_muls / rho_matched_muls on every record (checks above).
rho_reference_assessment.strongest_available: on all 22 curves j(E) is outside F_{p^2} (independent Python check: j^(p^2) != j; the generators also reject j in F_{p^2}), so no Frobenius-type endomorphism is defined over F_{p^4} and Aut(E) = {+-1}: negation is the strongest fold. Negation walks take 0.71-1.16 sqrt(n) steps (16-walk means over the 22 curves), against sqrt(pi n / 4) = 0.886 sqrt(n).
rho_reference_assessment.same_unit_and_process: the walks (rho4_folded) run in the same process after the index calculus (collect_and_solve), on the same instance, with the same Fp4/Curve4 counters.
rho_reference_assessment.unpriced_native_work: Read from src/cryptanalysis/quartic_folds.rs, klein_v4.rs, d4_weighted_s5.rs and gaudry_quartic.rs: the index calculus charges F_p multiplications only (the Fp4 counter: an F_{p^4} multiplication 19, an inversion 40; the solve's F_p multiplications counted directly; the matrix at 16 per mod-n multiplication). Unpriced on the index calculus: the Macaulay matrices' entry traffic and additions (emitted: macaulay_entries, rows x cols at each call's last degree), the solve's F_p inversions (inv_mod per pivot or eigenvector; count not emitted, at most one per pivot row, far fewer than the entries), hash and table work in the lift-back, F_p additions. Unpriced on the walks: per step the hash-table lookup and insert, the partition hashes (two with the look-ahead) and the class comparisons, F_p additions (emitted: steps). The protocol's band prices one GAE per Macaulay entry and one per walk step, GAE = the curve's measured F_p multiplications per affine addition (fp_muls_per_add = 97.0 on every record). Native work is unpriced on both arms, so the 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE values differ.
limitations: 16 walks per curve: the matched-walk mean carries roughly 13 % sampling error (coefficient of variation about 0.5 / sqrt(16)); per-curve S/rho inherits it.

The walk's mean includes its set-up (32 random multiples), which dominates at small n (S_rho per sqrt n 243 at p = 53 against 92 at p = 269 for E19); this makes rho dearer at small n and the IC/rho ratio lower there.

The E19 -> E24 factor (35-240x) is the 0 GAE value; at 1 GAE per native operation it is 6.5-45x (E24's Macaulay entries per call weigh more against its smaller C); E24 stays below E19 at every matched (p, seed) at every price.
The handovers (2^116.7, 2^90.1) are section 11.16's model extrapolated with theory exponents from measured constants, not measured crossings.
